title: I Photographed Her Parents as They Were Sentenced for Her Twin’s Death. Years Later, I Photographed Her Life.
author: Beth Nakamura
content:
About eight years ago, I was assigned to photograph the sentencing of Travis
and Sarah Mitchell, a couple with deep roots in an insular faith-healing sect
outside of Portland, Oregon.  

The Mitchells, as members of the Followers of Christ, adhere to a doctrine
that forbids medical care. Instead, followers rely on healing through faith.
So when Sarah Mitchell gave birth prematurely to twins in 2017 — and both
gasped for breath in their first hours — the couple didn’t rush them to an
emergency room. Instead, they turned to prayer.

One twin, Ginnifer, lived for four hours, each one a struggle. The family
eventually sought medical care for her surviving twin sister, Evelyn, but only
after the county’s deputy medical examiner arrived at the location of the home
birth and learned, though not right away, of Evelyn’s existence. Even then, he
had to seek help from police, who arrived at the Oregon City home and told
reluctant family members to take the struggling infant to the hospital or
they’d do it themselves.

The Mitchells pleaded guilty to criminally negligent homicide in the death of
their infant daughter, Ginnifer, and to criminal mistreatment for failing to
seek medical care for her surviving twin, Evelyn. The couple’s lawyer told the
judge that the Mitchells grieved the loss of Ginnifer and loved Evelyn.
“Travis and Sarah are utterly sincere, decent and caring human beings,” he
told the judge. (The Mitchells and their lawyer did not respond to ProPublica
and The Oregonian’s recent requests to be interviewed.)

Today, my memory of the sentencing is more montage than detail. But I remember
the crowded gallery, the couple in black-and-white-striped prison clothing,
and their prison sentence of more than six years. Evelyn, who within days of
her birth had been placed in the custody of Marshall and Jennifer Phillips,
another couple in the Followers of Christ, wasn’t present. She remained in the
couple’s permanent care.

The Mitchells went off to prison, and I went on with my life.

Such is the grinding rhythm of the daily news cycle. So often I see people on
their worst day — and then never again. Stories don’t really end, of course,
but my role as a photojournalist is limited. I’m an observer rather than a
participant, seeing mostly slivers of the human experience that offer only a
window into the whole. It’s rare that I get to see what happens next.

Never would I have dreamed that the surviving baby in this case, Evelyn, would
be someone I’d later come to know and care about through my work. But that’s
precisely what happened eight years after that courtroom scene played out,
when I began documenting the lives of Evelyn and her parents, the Phillipses.
(In a legal filing in an ongoing case relating to Evelyn’s custody, the
Mitchells criticized the Phillipses for allowing her to participate in our
coverage.)**** The [resulting
story](https://www.propublica.org/article/followers-of-christ-oregon-city-
evelyn-marshall-phillips), a collaboration between ProPublica and The
Oregonian, is one of several recently published about faith healing and the
Followers of Christ church. It intimately explores the Phillipses’ journey out
of the sect and illustrates how changes in Oregon state law — in contrast to
neighboring Idaho, [where the Followers have a handful of
churches](https://www.propublica.org/article/faith-healing-idaho-deaths-
followers-of-christ) — have led to a reduction in child deaths.

To spend time around 9-year-old Evelyn is to behold a luminous, magnetic force
of nature. It’s impossible to imagine this same girl as a premature baby so
small that the only items that fit her were doll clothes purchased from the
supermarket toy aisle.

For months, as I documented Evelyn’s life — from her baptism to her home life
to doctors’ appointments — my journalism colleagues worked on their own pieces
of our project. Teresa Mahoney, video editor at The Oregonian, produced [a
video introduction to the story](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kM6Ewe9rkGc)
that included a sequence of footage recorded by body cameras worn by police
officers who stood outside Evelyn’s grandparents’ house that night, at first
nudging, then ordering, Evelyn’s family to get her to the hospital. Each time
I viewed it, as I watched the officers politely letting time slip away, I’d
need to regulate my own breathing as I imagined Evelyn on the other side of
that door, struggling to breathe herself.

I hope that reporter Noelle Crombie’s words, Teresa’s video and my photographs
allow readers to see not only the journey of the couple who are raising Evelyn
as their own but also the surviving — indeed, thriving — twin I came to know.
That Evelyn is alive at all is, depending on your worldview, a miracle.

My work is all about observing and capturing moments, about freezing time.
Here, I was witnessing the unfolding of time. I got to see what happened next.

![A man with short white hair wears a white polo shirt and stands waist deep
in a green tank of water. He dunks a girl wearing a white dress into the
water. He places his hand over her own hand as she holds her nose. A drum set,
microphone and music stand can be seen next to the
tank.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ-
Oregon2431_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Evelyn’s
baptism was a highly anticipated day and meaningful for all involved. The
stakes were high for me because the immersion lasted only a few seconds. I had
one chance to get it right.  ![A girl wearing sparkly red buckled shoes and a
white dress sits on a gray stool with her hands in her lap. A woman wearing a
black and white floral print dress stands barefoot with painted toenails
beside her. The photo shows the two people only from the waist down. The floor
is brown tile.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ2891_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Jennifer
Phillips is a steadfast presence in Evelyn’s life. This moment of her curling
Evelyn’s hair in preparation for the baptism reminded me of daguerreotypes
from the 1800s. In some, mothers who wanted photographs of their babies had to
hold them behind velvet drapes so as not to be visible in the portraits. I
thought of the nature of emotional labor and how much of it is unseen. ![A man
wearing a black shirt squeezes his eyes shut and smiles while a girl next to
him grins broadly and throws her head back. Brown, yellow and red wallpaper
decorates a nearby wall and out-of-focus bright white lights are reflected in
the glass wall behind them.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-Christ-
Oregon2399_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Evelyn
was getting a kick out of giving Marshall a pounding back massage. We were all
at McDonald’s — her favorite restaurant — having her birthday meal. ![A man
wearing a black suit, dress shoes and a white shirt extends one hand out while
his other hand holds the hand of a girl with long brown hair wearing a blue
tiered dress, frilly white socks and sparkly red buckle shoes. They are
dancing on a shiny basketball court and are lit up by pink, green and blue
lighting. Glowing lanterns hang from the
ceiling.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Daddy-
daughter-
dance956_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Marshall
Phillips and Evelyn attended a father-daughter dance at a high school a few
towns away. Evelyn had a list of dances she and Marshall practiced. I had
recently lost my father and was carrying grief. But seeing Marshall’s love for
Evelyn was beautiful and healing. ![A girl with a red bow in her long brown
hair and wearing a blue dress smiles as she looks into a gold hand mirror.
Pink, purple and white face paint decorates her
forehead.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Daddy-
daughter-
dance961_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)In
person, Evelyn sparkles. When she saw herself in a mirror with her face
painted, her delight was electric. ![A girl puts a pink helmet over her head
as a man arranges a garland with letters spelling “under the sea.” They are
standing in front of a sheet hanging over a wall, partially covering family
photos. Another person’s hand reaches out from the
side.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ-
Oregon2392_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)The
night before Evelyn’s ninth birthday party, the family decorated the room
where the event would take place. I know firsthand how much parenting involves
endless tasks and routines. Mixed into the chaos are moments of pure joy. ![A
hand with light nail polish holds an orange, black and purple stethoscope to a
girl’s heart. The girl is wearing a light blue striped patient gown with the
sleeves rolled up and a gold necklace with “Evelyn” as the
pendant.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ-
Oregon2463_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Yearly
pediatric check-ups are an ordinary aspect of childhood, and for Evelyn it’s
no different. Knowing her history, however, gives these moments an undeniable
poignance. A check on her heart rate becomes a reminder of the miracle of her
very existence. ![A man closes his eyes and clasps his hands over a woman
lying in bed holding a little girl who also closes her eyes and clasps her
hands. The bed is small and has a white metal frame. A child’s drawing of two
people standing on grass hangs next to the bed on the
wall.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ2884_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Before
bed, Marshall reads a chapter book to Evelyn that combines the concept of
evolution with lessons from the Bible. Evelyn was excited I was there and
sprinkled in knock-knock jokes between the biblical passages. After that, the
family prays together. ![Four girls wearing dresses dance in a line on a gym
floor, with their hands on one another’s shoulders. The room is dimly lit in
red and blue, and adults cast shadows on the padded wall behind the
dancers.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Followers-of-
Christ2876_preview_maxWidth_3000_maxHeight_3000_ppi_72_embedColorProfile_true_quality_95.jpg)Although
Evelyn didn’t know the other kids at the father-daughter dance, she seemed to
make friends easily. Here, she formed a conga line with a group of girls.

The post [I Photographed Her Parents as They Were Sentenced for Her Twin’s
Death. Years Later, I Photographed Her
Life.](https://www.propublica.org/article/faith-healing-child-photo-essay)
appeared first on [ProPublica](https://www.propublica.org).
